episodes.162080: A Pacific cold frontal system pushed through the area during the morning of October 8 spreading widespread precipitation across the area. Several stations in the eastern portion of the San Joaquin Valley and the Sierra Nevada range measured between a tenth and a four tenths of an inch of rainfall with portions of Fresno and Madera Counties picking up locally heavy showers which produced higher precipitation amounts. Several high elevation SNOTELs picked up an estimated one to three inches of new snowfall. The precipitation ended by late afternoon as the storm moved east of the area.
episodes.162108: Early morning strong to isolated severe storms formed ahead of a frontal boundary over a moist and moderately unstable airmass with passing level short wave trough energy aloft. An outflow boundary ahead of the small MCS-like cluster of storms pressed southward during the late morning and afternoon hours which further convective enhancement, triggering pulse strong to severe storms.

episodes.162235: Numerous thunderstorms developed in the afternoon and evening hours and produced strong wind gusts along and offshore of the east central Florida coast, spanning from Daytona Beach to near Ft. Pierce. Two waterspouts were also observed just offshore of Volusia county, one being east of Daytona Beach and the other being east of Bethune Beach.
episodes.162447: An upper level disturbance passing through the Great Lakes region and the Ohio Valley led to an abundance of moisture streaming into West Virginia on October 8th. An increase in moisture coupled with daytime heating resulted in showers and thunderstorms that crossed through the central portions of the state. The slow moving orientation of these showers and storms caused a few instances of localized flooding in Putnam and Kanawha Counties, resulting in impassable roadways that evening.
episodes.162453: An upper level disturbance passing through the Great Lakes region and the Ohio Valley led to an abundance of moisture streaming into Kentucky on October 8th. An increase in moisture coupled with daytime heating resulted in showers and thunderstorms that crossed through the central portions of the state. The slow moving orientation of these showers and storms caused a few instances of localized flooding in Greenup County, resulting high water flowing up to the first step of local residential homes and businesses in the town of Russell.
episodes.162463: A strong mid-level shortwave tracking over the region led to thunderstorms capable of producing strong to severe winds across coastal waters.
episodes.162958: Isolated severe thunderstorms developed along a warm front across central Georgia. These storms combined with a saturated atmosphere to produce high rainfall rates over the state, with the highest accumulations over central and eastern Georgia causing flash flooding.
episodes.163228: A strong cold front moved through the area during the morning hours of October 8th.  A line of strong to briefly severe thunderstorms slowly moved through portions of south-central Georgia, bringing a few trees down and flash flooding to portions of Ben Hill and Irwin counties.
episodes.163301: Central Kentucky was located in the warm sector ahead of a surface low to the west, a west to east oriented warm front to the north, and a north to south oriented cold front to the southwest. Moderate instability and shear from strong southern flow took advantage of the added Gulf of Mexico moisture. This produced thunderstorms that caused isolated severe wind damage and flash flooding over the two day period.
episodes.163526: A funnel cloud was reported by the public just south of Jamestown.
episodes.163646: A thunderstorm dumped at least 4 inches of rain in less than 2 hours, leading to flash flooding in Orion Township.  Roads were damaged, cars submerged and stranded, and homes flooded. Flood waters impacted the M-24 and I-75 interchange, with roads closed for several hours.
episodes.163813: A slow moving area of upper level low pressure over the Mid-Mississippi Valley continued to pump semi-tropical moisture into the western Carolinas resulting in another round of locally heavy rainfall across Upstate South Carolina. Heavy rainfall of 2 to 4 inches over the span of a few hours on an already wet ground resulted in flash flooding developing along the Reedy River in the city of Greenville.
episodes.163898: A storm system brought flash flooding and high winds to portions of southern Utah and severe thunderstorm wind gusts to portions of northern Utah.

events.narrative: The intersection of Broadway and Washington was closed due to flooding.
Ecton Road was closed due to flooding.
The Fremont Island automated weather station recorded a peak wind gust of 69 mph. Severe wind gusts lasted 10 minutes.
The emergency manager reported that roads were closed and water rescues were taking place.
A large tree was downed in Ogden.
A layer of asphalt was washed away on Creekside Lane. Four Mile Road was closed due to flood damage.
The RAWs station near Baxley measured a storm total rainfall of 2.02 inches since morning.
A rain gauge near Baxley measured 2.29 inches of rainfall since early morning.
The Jacksonville (JAX) ASOS measured a storm total rainfall of 2.21 inches as of 1:32 pm.
The Naval Station Mayport AWOS measured a storm total rainfall of 2.63 inches. The time duration was estimated.
The Laurens County Emergency Manager reported several trees blown down across the county from around Montrose to near Cedar Grove.
Two pine trees were blown down across Highway 206.
A tree was blown down across the highway in Osierfield.
The Walmart parking lot flooded to a depth of 1 to 2 feet in places.  Numerous cars were stalled or stranded.  Behind the Walmart, some cars parked near an adjacent creek floated in the flood waters.
One home flooded in the 500 block of South Thomas Road.  Water was 2 inches deep inside.  Another unoccupied building nearby flooded as well.
An observer measured 2.15 inches of rainfall in less than 2 hours.
An observer measured 3.21 inches of rainfall in 90 minutes.

County EM reported a mobile home was destroyed by straight line winds along Guy Pridgen Road near Bowens Mill Road and GA Highway 268. Numerous trees were blown down in the area and a barn was damaged by fallen trees. The time of damage was based on radar.

There were reports of significant flooding around Fitzgerald High school extending west across Merrimack Drive.  The water depth was reported up to the doors of vehicles and up to the front door of a double wide mobile home.
The underpass on North Longstreet was flooded with a car submerged.
Several roads were flooded and closed in eastern Irwin county due to flooding in the Osierfield area.
A trained spotted reported heavy rainfall for almost two hours in north Fresno and Clovis with ponding of water reported on several roadways.
A few trees were blown down in the southeast portion of the county. The time of damage was based on radar.
An observer measured 1.25 inches of rainfall in a short duration which caused minor street flooding. The time was estimated.

A stream gauge on the Reedy River in west Greenville indicated flash flooding developed along a portion of the river after 2 to 4 inches fell in just a few hours. This indicated significant flooding of low-lying areas along portions of the Swamp Rabbit Trail and Hudson St.  Cleveland Park and Lakehurst St also flooded due to backwater effects along Richland Creek. Backwater effects along Long Branch Creek flooded low-lying areas near Westside Park and Lily St. Additionally, the media reported inundation of Pine Grove Ln in Berea due to flooding along a tributary of the Reedy.
